name: Should I replace the vanity or refinish it in a guest bathroom remodel?

mainEntity.name: Is it better to replace a guest bathroom vanity or refinish the one that is already there?
mainEntity.text: Is it better to replace a guest bathroom vanity or refinish the one that is already there?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whether to replace or refinish a vanity depends on structure, layout, and design goals. If the cabinet is solid and the size still works well, refinishing can save money and preserve time for other upgrades. That can be a smart move in a guest bathroom where the vanity does not need to be oversized or highly custom. Replacing the vanity makes more sense when the current piece is damaged, too shallow, poorly sized, or awkwardly aligned with the sink and plumbing. A new vanity can also improve storage and give the room a more modern profile. In small bathrooms, the vanity shape matters because it affects circulation and visual openness. If the countertop, sink style, or plumbing line needs to change anyway, replacement may be the cleaner solution. The best choice is the one that improves function without adding unnecessary work.
acceptedAnswer.description: Replace the vanity if the size, storage, or condition no longer works. Refinish or repaint it if the cabinet is solid, the style still fits, and you mainly want a cleaner look. Vanity condition, plumbing alignment, and countertop compatibility should guide the decision.
